extracted.intended_audience: management liability professionals, corporate lawyers, D&O insurance practitioners, and corporate governance observers
extracted.subtask_description: A blog-post case analysis of the November 4, 2019 WeWork shareholder complaint that discusses alleged fiduciary breaches, transactional self-dealing, class/derivative claims, and implications for private-company D&O insurance. It summarizes allegations, legal theories, and practical insurance/management lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breach of fiduciary duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint asserts claims for breach of fiduciary duty on behalf of the company (derivative) and the minority shareholders (class).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gist: Neumann, in concert with SoftBank, used their control of the company to the benefit of themselves and to the detriment of the minority shareholders and of the company; the board allegedly aided and abetted this misconduct. Use factual allegations showing misuse of control, preferential treatment, or decisions that harm minority shareholders to support such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aiding and abetting breach of fiduciary duty
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint alleges the company’s board of directors aided and abetted Neumann’s alleged fiduciary breaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pointers: Show board knowledge or participation in the challenged transactions or a failure to act where a duty existed; the complaint treats board involvement as a separate actionable theory alongside direct fiduciary breach claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate waste
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint includes a claim of corporate waste based on allegedly excessive or unnecessary payments/benefits to insiders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: termination package elements (share sale rights, loan repayments, large consulting fee) alleged to be disproportionate and to provide no corporate benefit. Corporate waste claims focus on value given away with no reasonable corporate purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory and injunctive relief (including blocking buybacks)
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint seeks declaratory and injunctive relief and specifically asks the court to block further buybacks of minority shareholders’ shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief-seeking strategy: In addition to monetary damages, seek injunctions to prevent consummation of transactions or further actions (e.g., buybacks) that perpetuate alleged harm to minority shareholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abuse of control / grossly unfair offering price
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint alleges the offering share price is 'grossly unfair' and represents 'an abuse of control' by Neumann and SoftBank, resulting in 'unfair treatment of minority shareholders.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on disparity between insider-favorable terms and minority-offered consideration, and on how control was used to depress price or obtain unfair terms. Alleging unfairness to minorities supports fiduciary and related claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-dealing / improper personal payment
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint is highly critical of Neumann’s $185 million 'consulting fee,' calling it 'self-dealing and an improper personal payment to Neumann.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations should show the payment personally benefits the insider without legitimate corporate purpose and that transaction approvals were tainted by conflicted interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation disparity in insider termination package
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint notes that valuation Neumann will get for his shares is superior to the consideration being offered to the minority shareholders (part of the alleged extraction of benefits worth $1.7 billion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete comparisons of how insiders are treated versus minority holders (e.g., price per share, liquidity opportunities) to show preferential treatment and harm to minorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure-to-launch (IPO failure) as a basis for litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the claimant’s grievances is the company’s failure to complete the IPO — described as a 'failure to launch' claim tied to the events surrounding the aborted offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lesson: adverse events in the IPO process can spawn litigation alleging that insider conduct caused or exploited the failed offering; consider how pre-IPO actions and disclosures bear on duties and claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private companies can face shareholder class action litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though WeWork was and is a privately-held company, the complaint represents a class action lawsuit — a reminder that private companies can be hit with shareholder litigation, including investor class actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical note for practitioners and insurers: Do not assume class/derivative risk is limited to public companies; private 'unicorns' are exposed to investor litigation risks tied to valuation, governance, and large financing events.

rubrics_metrics.name: D&O insurance coverage consideration — Securities Claim exclusion wording
rubrics_metrics.description: When structuring pre-IPO private company D&O insurance, the policy’s Securities Claim exclusion must be worded so it does not preclude coverage for 'failure to launch' or similar private-company shareholder claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insurance implication: Insurers and brokers should ensure Securities Claim exclusions and other exclusions are carefully drafted so that private-company shareholder suits (including class/derivative claims tied to IPO events) remain within coverage where intended.
